notes.text: Since the normal opposition is between "living" (i.e., "fresh and flowing") water and tahmia water, we wonder as to the complete appropriateness of the commonly accepted rendering "turbid", for surely flowing water can be turbid, while neither stagnant water nor turbid water would qualify as "living" for the Mandaeans. For further discusssion and the view of others who would connect this term with thwm, thwmɁ n.m. "abyss" see Băncilǎ (2018) pp. 106ff. But given the regular alternation between tmh and thm and the regular semantic connection between "to be amazed" and "to stand still" in West Semitic , we see little reason to doubt our etymology and our primary definition.
